subtitle: Where river dust, fire and stone birthed steel for distant worlds

panels.shot: epic wide aerial over dry river plain dotted with furnaces and huts
panels.action: A sweeping view of Kodumanal on the Noyyal River shows clusters of mud-brick furnaces, smoke rising into a pale sky, workers as small silhouettes moving among bead workshops and iron-smelting yards.

dialogue.text: In the Sangam age at Kodumanal, far from palaces, Tamil craftsmen forged iron and steel that would travel the world.

i18n.hi: संगम युग का कोडुमनाल, महलों से दूर, जहां तमिल कारीगरों ने लोहा और इस्पात गढ़ा जो दुनिया घूमने वाला था।

panels.action: A dusty track runs across scrubland towards Kodumanal’s clustered houses; to one side the shallow Noyyal River glints, to the other caravans of pack bullocks move, laden with bales and jars.

dialogue.text: Kodumanal, known in old songs as Kodumanam, stood on an inland route linking Malabar’s spice ports with the Coromandel coast.

i18n.hi: पुराने गीतों का कोडुमनम, जो मलाबार के मसाला बंदरगाहों को कोरोमंडल तट से जोड़ने वाले भीतरी रास्ते पर खड़ा था।

panels.shot: slow push-in toward the settlement edge
panels.action: Kodumanal Ironworker stands at the edge of the town, watching traders arrive: men with turbans and dhotis, a foreigner in a short cloak, baskets of pepper and cloth piled high on animals.

dialogue.text: Here traders brought spices, cloth and coins, and carried away beads and iron from workshops that hummed day and night.

i18n.hi: यहां व्यापारी मसाले, कपड़ा और सिक्के लाते, और मोती व लोहा लेकर जाते, उन कारखानों से जो दिन–रात गूंजते रहते।

panels.action: Within the industrial quarter, Kodumanal Ironworker moves through a yard of clay furnaces, stacks of ore nodules, heaps of charcoal, and rows of stone drills, as other artisans grind carnelian and shape shell bangles.

dialogue.text: Excavations reveal dense industrial life: furnaces, crucibles, ore, carnelian beads and shell, all crowded into a working town.

i18n.hi: खुदाइयों में दिखती है घनी औद्योगिक जिंदगी: भट्टियां, कुंड, अयस्क, कार्नेलियन के मोती और शंख, सब मिलकर एक कामकाजी नगर में ठुंसे हुए।

panels.shot: medium shot beside a furnace, warm glow
panels.action: Kodumanal Ironworker stands near a low clay furnace, face lit by its orange glow, as another worker uses a simple bellows to drive air through a tuyere; behind them, slag and broken crucibles lie in piles.

dialogue.text: Ironworkers built small furnaces, fed them ore and charcoal, and learned to control fire and air with practised hands.

i18n.hi: लोहारे छोटी भट्टियां बनाते, उनमें अयस्क और कोयला डालते, और सीखी हुई हथेलियों से आग और हवा को काबू में रखते।

panels.shot: close-up on hands sorting ores and charcoal
panels.action: Kodumanal Ironworker crouches, hands selecting dense iron-rich nodules from a basket, measuring charcoal by eye, while crucibles sit ready, lined up on a flat stone.

dialogue.text: Through trial, tradition and guild memory, they knew which ores, which charcoal, and how much heat would yield strong metal.

i18n.hi: कई कोशिशों, परंपरा और संघ की याद से उन्हें पता था कौन सा अयस्क, कौन सा कोयला, कितनी गर्मी से मजबूत धातु बनती है।

panels.shot: dramatic low-angle focused on crucibles in the furnace
panels.action: Several small closed crucibles stand inside a larger furnace; Kodumanal Ironworker leans in, eyes narrowed, as flames lick around the clay vessels, smoke spiralling upward into the dim workshop roof.

dialogue.text: South Indian smiths refined blooms of iron into high-carbon steel in sealed crucibles, an art later known as urukku and ukku.

i18n.hi: दक्षिण भारतीय लोहार लोहे की गाठों को बंद कुंडों में शुद्ध कर उच्च कार्बन इस्पात बनाते, जिसे बाद में उरुक्कु और उक्कु कहा गया।

panels.shot: extreme close-up on the ironworker’s sweat-lined face
panels.action: Sweat beads on Kodumanal Ironworker’s brow as he listens to the roar of the furnace, palms hovering near the heat to sense its strength, his expression calm but intensely focused.

dialogue.text: Too cool, and the metal dies. Too hot, and it shatters.

i18n.hi: कम गर्मी तो धातु मर जाती। ज्यादा गर्मी तो चकनाचूर।

panels.shot: medium shot of crucibles being withdrawn
panels.action: Kodumanal Ironworker uses long tongs to lift a glowing crucible from the furnace mouth, carefully placing it on the ground to cool; fellow workers stand back, shielding their faces from the heat.

dialogue.text: From such furnaces came compact cakes of steel, small in size but rich in carbon and trusted by armourers far away.

i18n.hi: ऐसी भट्टियों से निकले इस्पात के छोटे, सघन लोइए, आकार में छोटे पर कार्बन से भरपूर, जिन पर दूर के शस्त्रकार भरोसा करते।

panels.shot: close-up of cooled steel cake beside beads and tools
panels.action: On a stone slab lies a dark, solid steel cake, next to carnelian beads, iron chisels and a Tamil Brahmi-inscribed potsherd; Kodumanal Ironworker’s hand rests near them as if weighing their worth.

dialogue.text: Archaeologists find slag, crucibles and steel residues here, alongside Tamil Brahmi sherds that speak of organized production and accounting.

i18n.hi: पुरातत्वविद यहां भस्म, कुंड और इस्पात के अवशेष पाते हैं, साथ ही तमिल ब्राह्मी के टुकड़े जो संगठित उत्पादन और लेखे–जोखे की गवाही देते हैं।

panels.shot: wide shot of bustling yard with traders and artisans
panels.action: In the yard, bead-makers drill stones, a scribe marks signs on pottery, and Kodumanal Ironworker shows a steel cake to a visiting merchant who inspects it with practiced eyes.

dialogue.text: This is no common iron. It cuts and lasts.

i18n.hi: ये साधारण लोहा नहीं। काटता भी है, टिकता भी है।

panels.shot: medium shot with a foreign trader offering a coin
panels.action: A foreign trader with short beard and cloak holds out a Roman coin toward Kodumanal Ironworker, while pointing at bundles of beads and ingots stacked nearby; other local traders look on.

dialogue.text: Roman coins and imported ware at Kodumanal show how its goods entered wider circuits, moving towards ports and distant buyers.

i18n.hi: कोडुमनाल में मिले रोमन सिक्के और बाहरी सामान बताते हैं कि यहां की चीजें बड़े घेरों में घुसकर बंदरगाहों और दूर के खरीदारों तक पहुंचती थीं।

panels.shot: bird’s-eye view of caravan departing town
panels.action: A caravan of bullocks and carts leaves Kodumanal along the dusty road, carrying sacks, jars and wrapped metal pieces, as Kodumanal Ironworker watches from a rise above the town.

dialogue.text: From inland nodes like Kodumanal, steel, iron tools and beads joined larger flows towards Chera and Pandya ports.

i18n.hi: कोडुमनाल जैसे भीतरी ठिकानों से इस्पात, लोहे के औज़ार और मोती मिलकर बड़े बहावों में चेऱ और पांड्य बंदरगाहों की तरफ बढ़ते थे।

panels.shot: montage-style wide panel showing ships at sea
panels.action: On a distant coast, stitched wooden ships ride grey-green waves; on the deck, bales of pepper, bundles of textiles and small packages of metal are lashed under a restless sky.

dialogue.text: Along the western and eastern coasts, such cargoes met ocean ships bound for Arabia, the Mediterranean and island realms.

i18n.hi: पश्चिमी और पूर्वी तटों पर ऐसी खेपें उन समुद्री जहाजों से मिलतीं जो अरब, भूमध्यसागर और द्वीपी राज्यों को जा रहे होते।

panels.shot: split visual: South Indian furnace vs Sri Lankan furnace
panels.action: On one side of the panel, a South Indian-style crucible furnace glows; on the other, a similar furnace in a Sri Lankan landscape burns, linking two traditions across the sea.

dialogue.text: Modern studies trace crucible steel remains in south India and Sri Lanka, showing related high-carbon techniques across the region.

i18n.hi: आधुनिक शोध दक्षिण भारत और श्रीलंका में मिले कुंड–इस्पात के अवशेषों को जोड़ते हैं, दिखाते हैं कि पूरे क्षेत्र में जुड़ी उच्च कार्बन तकनीकें थीं।

panels.shot: close-up of a finished sword blade in a foreign workshop
panels.action: In a distant workshop beyond India, an armourer holds a polished sword blade, its surface finely finished, as small steel cakes lie on a bench, hinting at their journey from southern furnaces.

dialogue.text: Indian crucible steel became famed as a raw material, worked elsewhere into blades that later travellers called wondrous.

i18n.hi: भारतीय कुंड–इस्पात कच्चे माल के रूप में मशहूर हुआ, जिसे दूर देशों में गढ़कर उन धारों में बदला गया जिन्हें बाद के यात्री चमत्कारी कह गए।

panels.shot: quiet medium shot of the ironworker at dusk
panels.action: At dusk in Kodumanal, the furnace fires have dimmed; Kodumanal Ironworker sits on a stone, hands resting, looking at the cooling workshop with a tired but steady gaze.

dialogue.text: My name may fade. The work will endure.

i18n.hi: नाम मिट भी जाए, काम तो रहेगा।

panels.action: Centuries later, archaeologists in hats and simple clothes kneel in a trench at Kodumanal, brushing around furnace remains, crucibles, beads and a Roman coin embedded in the soil profile.

dialogue.text: Excavations at Kodumanal uncover industrial debris and trade relics, letting us read this town’s role in ancient networks.

i18n.hi: कोडुमनाल की खुदाइयों से फैला कारखाना–कचरा और व्यापार की चीजें निकलती हैं, जो हमें इस नगर की जगह पुराने जालों में पढ़ने देती हैं।

panels.shot: symbolic wide shot blending past furnaces with modern lab
panels.action: The panel blends Kodumanal’s glowing ancient furnaces on one side with a modern laboratory on the other, where a scientist studies steel residues; Kodumanal Ironworker’s silhouette stands between them.

dialogue.text: Kodumanal’s iron workers show that great innovations can rise in crowded workshops along trade routes, far from royal courts, yet shape weapons and tools across continents and centuries.

i18n.hi: कोडुमनाल के लोहे के कामगार दिखाते हैं कि बड़ी खोजें राजदरबारों से नहीं, व्यापार–रास्तों के किनारे भरी–भरी दुकानों में भी जन्म लेती हैं, और फिर महाद्वीपों व सदियों तक हथियारों और औज़ारों को आकार देती हैं।

title_i18n.en: The Sword That Crossed the World
title_i18n.hi: वो तलवार जो दुनिया पार कर गई

subtitle_i18n.en: Where river dust, fire and stone birthed steel for distant worlds
subtitle_i18n.hi: जहां नदी की मिट्टी, आग और पत्थर ने दूर जगतों के लिए इस्पात जन्मा
